canvas-02-1.description: The north part of Glen Gardner, on printed sheet 1 of the September 1921 atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Main Street runs down the middle of the part from the iron bridge over Spruce Run, past the Howard Mains silk throwing mill, the Glen Gardner Hotel and a row of stores and dwellings, to the bottom edge where it continues on the next sheet. Hampton Road, also called North Main, runs north from Sodom Road on the west side of Spruce Run, and Main runs north on the east side; both continue into the inset at the top. Sodom Road crosses the part from the west past the public school to the iron bridge, with West Street leaving it to the south. Changewater Road forks north-east from Main above the hotel, and Hill Road leaves Main eastward and crosses the C.R.R. of N.J. tracks, which run down the east side of the part. The First Lutheran Church stands on Hampton Road at the top; the lower part of Main has dwellings, a blacksmith, a barber, auto repair shops, a post office and John T. Force's agricultural implement store. Farm buildings, barns and wagon houses are scattered in the open blocks numbered 1, 2, 27 and 28. Spruce Run curves through the part from top to bottom. The title cartouche, water and fire notes, legend and location map, the inset at the top and the separately drawn sanatorium are outside this part.
notes: Sodom Road is today School Street; Changewater Road is Bell Avenue; Hampton Road keeps its name.

Placed from Hampton Road / School Street and Hill Road / Main Street (detected) and Bell Avenue / Main Street (hand-picked); three points only. The fitted scale is 5 percent above the printed scale bar (3.96 px/ft), which is set in the config so the second pass holds it.
West Street has no counterpart among today's named streets.

canvas-02-2.description: A small inset in a heavy-ruled box at the top of printed sheet 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing to the upper right. It continues Main and Hampton Road north of the main map: the two roads run up side by side from the bottom edge, marked 1 to show they continue on the main map, and merge into a single 45-foot road that leaves the inset at the top. Spruce Run crosses the upper right corner. Only a few buildings are drawn: a cider press with a gasoline engine, two outbuildings east of Main, a dwelling at the top and a building on a large lot west of Hampton Road. Block number 2 lies east of Main.
notes: Placed on the single junction where Hampton Road and Main Street merge, with the printed scale and the rotation of the main part of the sheet (anchored, low confidence).

sheet-1-1.description: The centre of Glen Gardner on printed sheet 2 of the September 1921 atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Main runs down the middle from the top edge, where it continues from the inset, to Hillside Avenue and on to its fork with Church Street, then south-west across Spruce Run on a long bridge to Mack Avenue. Hillside Avenue crosses Main and the C.R.R. of N.J. tracks; west of Main it crosses Spruce Run on a plank bridge to Mack Avenue and High Street, east of the tracks it passes the town hall and continues east beside 2nd Street. Railroad Avenue runs south from Hillside Avenue along the east side of the tracks and turns east into Mountain Lane. The railroad station and freight house stand beside the tracks, the M.E. Church on Church Street and the Presbyterian church on Mack Avenue; The Maples stands at the south-west corner. Main is lined with dwellings, auto sheds, a job printing shop, general stores and an auto repair shop. A stream runs east through the blocks between Hillside Avenue and Mountain Lane. The inset at the lower right is a separate part.
notes: Hillside Avenue west of Main is today Sanatorium Road and east of the tracks part of Railroad Avenue; Railroad Avenue keeps its name; Mack Avenue lies on or near today's NJ 31.

Placed from Main Street / Sanatorium Road and Railroad Avenue / Sanatorium Road (detected) and Church Street / Main Street and Mountain Lane / Railroad Avenue (hand-picked). The fitted scale is 3.5 percent below the printed scale bar (3.96 px/ft), which is set in the config.
The north arrow points about 20 degrees further clockwise than the fitted rotation.

Part 2 inset at lower right: Main between the bottom of sheet 1 and the top of the main map.

sheet-1-2.description: An inset in a heavy-ruled box at the lower right of printed sheet 2, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows the stretch of Main between the bottom of sheet 1 and the top of the main map of sheet 2, marked 1 at the top and 2 at the bottom. Main runs down the middle with dwellings and outbuildings on both sides, a confectionery, auto sheds, storage buildings and an oven marked not used; a four-inch water pipe runs along the street. The C.R.R. of N.J. tracks run parallel on the east side and Spruce Run along the west edge, with block numbers 4 and 5.
notes: Placed from one point carried from the top of the main map of sheet 2, where the house numbers continue, with the printed scale and the bearing of today's Main Street (anchored, low confidence).
